intro.html:
a handheld mp3 player i built from scratch: circuit, firmware, and enclosure. this is the breadboard proof of concept. a custom pcba is next.

final spec:

> mp3 playback from microsd
> a dedicated i2s dac for audio out
> an eink display for track info and menus
> 5 buttons and a rotary encoder for navigation
> a usb-c rechargeable lipo
> all in a 3d printed enclosure

sections.label: scope
sections.html: the original list also had bluetooth out, line-in recording, and a speaker amp. i cut all three early. each one meant another radio, adc path, or power stage to debug, and none of them was needed to play music. with them gone, i could get the rest working reliably.

sections.label: architecture
sections.html:
the esp32 runs everything. i picked it for its hardware i2s peripheral and because it’s fast enough to decode mp3 in software, so i didn’t need a dedicated decoder chip.

> audio: the pcm5102a dac takes i2s from the esp32 (bck gpio22, lrck gpio21, din gpio27) and outputs line level stereo.

> display: a waveshare 2.13" eink (250x122, spi). i chose eink for power. it draws almost nothing once an image is on screen, so track info can stay up for hours.

> storage: a microsd module on the same spi bus as the display, with separate chip selects (display cs gpio5, sd cs gpio23).

> input: 5 tactile buttons for play/pause, skip, back, menu, and select, plus a rotary encoder for scrolling. the buttons sit on gpio34 to 39. those pins are input only and have no internal pull-ups, so each button has an external 10k pull-up to 3.3v.

> power: a tp4056 handles usb-c lipo charging. an mcp1700 ldo steps the battery’s 3.0 to 4.2v down to 3.3v.

sections.label: firmware
sections.html:
c++ on the arduino esp32 framework. it’s a state machine with four screens:

> now playing: track, artist, progress
> library: a scrollable list from the sd card
> menu
> settings: volume, display options

the esp32-audioI2S library decodes mp3 in software on the esp32’s dual core processor.

sections.label: problems
sections.html: > regulator dropout. my first regulator was an ams1117-3.3, which needs ~1v of headroom. that means 4.3v in for 3.3v out, more than a lipo gives for most of its discharge, so the device would have browned out with over half the battery left. i swapped to an mcp1700 with 178 mv dropout. it holds regulation down to ~3.48v, which covers almost the whole usable lipo range. during the swap a wiring error put the battery straight across the circuit and killed the first mcp1700. now i check polarity before a battery goes anywhere near the board.

> boot failures. i had put sd mosi on gpio12. the esp32 reads that pin at reset to set its flash voltage, so whenever the spi line pulled it high, boot failed at random. moving mosi to gpio23, which has no boot function, fixed it.

> sd module voltage. the first sd breakout had its own ams1117 onboard and expected 5v, so on the 3.3v rail it did nothing. i ran it from the 5v usb pin to keep testing, then switched to a 3.3v native module for the final build. that also got rid of a regulator a battery device had no use for.
> app size. the decoder library plus the display and sd code didn’t fit in the default partition. switching to the huge app partition scheme (3mb app, no ota) solved it.

sections.label: the dac problem
sections.html: this was the hardest bug in the project. with the dac wired and the i2s code running, i got no sound. even a plain 1 khz test tone was silent. the analog side was alive, because touching din to ground made a pop in the headphones. so the dac was powered and listening but never got usable audio.

i probed bck, lrck, and din on a scope. all three had clean signals at sensible frequencies and logic levels. that ruled out wiring and a dead i2s peripheral, but it also left me with hardware that looked correct and still didn’t work.

the cause was in software. esp32 arduino core 3.x rewrote the i2s driver, and the audio library hadn’t caught up. the driver started without errors and the clocks ran, but the data frames were wrong, so the dac got garbage and output nothing. rolling back to core 2.0.17, which uses the legacy driver/i2s.h the library was written against, fixed it with no code changes. sound came out on the first try.

a version mismatch like this fails quietly: the driver initializes and the scope shows clean signals, but the dac stays silent. now when something should work and doesn’t, i check version numbers before i touch hardware.

sections.label: audio output
sections.html: the pcm5102a outputs line level, ~2 vpp. that drives powered speakers fine, but its output impedance is too high to drive earbuds properly. a headphone amp stage between the dac and the jack would fix that, and it’s part of the pcba plan.

sections.label: prototype
sections.html: i tested each subsystem on its own before integration, in this order: power, sd, dac, display, then inputs. if five things fail at once you can’t tell which one is broken, so i only connected the next block after the current one worked.

sections.label: build
sections.html: the breadboard circuit sits in a 3d printed enclosure. the encoder knob and buttons are on the top face, the eink display sits in a recessed window, and the usb-c charging port is on the side.
